messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Purpose and access.** “The testing house may use the actuator drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, conduct and report on the agreed vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel named in a roster approved in writing by the Design Owner. Before receiving access, each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house remains responsible for their compliance. Advisers and subcontractors may receive access only if approved by name on the same terms.”

**Copies and fixtures.** “The testing house may make the minimum working copies needed for the tests and must encrypt them in transit and at rest. It may derive only the interface geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures for these tests. The drawings, copies, derived geometry and fixtures may not be used for another project or to develop or assist in developing a competing product.”

**Closeout and verification.** “Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the testing house must securely erase the drawings, CAD files and derived fixture files in its possession or under its control, including copies held by approved third parties. It must also destroy physical fixtures made from the geometry. By the same deadline, it must provide a certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials destroyed, the methods and dates of destruction, and any exceptions. The verifier may inspect records without receiving the CAD geometry. This certification satisfies the Design Owner’s verification requirement without site access.”

Can your backup systems meet the 30-day erasure deadline? If isolated backups must expire on a fixed cycle, please propose a maximum retention period and explain how you would prevent access and re-delete any files restored during that period. We can allow retention of the accepted test report if it contains no drawings or reconstructable geometry.

We can work with this structure. Three points need adjustment before we can sign the attachments: subcontractor substitution, backups, and the record-retention exception. Below is our replacement wording and the tradeoffs.

**1. Purpose and access — substitution and extracts**

Keep your first sentence and the roster/confidentiality flow-down. Replace "Advisers and subcontractors may receive access only if approved by name on the same terms" with:

> "Approved persons and firms may change during the job. The testing house may substitute test personnel or an approved third party (including its specialist machining shop and accredited test laboratory) by giving the Design Owner written notice of the replacement together with the same written confidentiality and use undertakings. The replacement is approved unless the Design Owner objects on reasonable grounds within five business days of notice. Access is suspended for the replaced person or firm from the date of notice and their deletion obligation runs from that date.
>
> Each approved third party receives only the minimum extract necessary for its task: the machining shop receives only the interface geometry required to fabricate the fixtures; the accredited laboratory receives only specimen, instrumentation and test-condition information needed to perform the calibrated testing. The testing house remains responsible for compliance by all approved persons and firms."

Rationale: a specialist can leave or be reassigned mid-job, and approval "by name" with no mechanism would stall testing at your cost as well as ours. The five-day objection window gives you real control without giving either of us a veto over scheduling. If you want a shorter window — three business days — we can live with that; what we cannot do is hold the job open for an undefined approval.

**2. Copies and fixtures — backup exception**

Your copies paragraph is acceptable as written. Add:

> "Backup exception: the testing house may retain disaster-recovery backup copies that are isolated from operational systems, not used in the ordinary course of business or to access drawing data, and held no longer than the fixed backup cycle. Maximum retention after the closeout deadline: **90 days**. Any file restored from backup is subject to the same deletion obligation and must be securely re-deleted within 10 business days of restoration, with the restoration and re-deletion reported in the closeout certificate. This is the sole exception to the 30-day erasure deadline."

This answers your question directly: yes, our backups cannot be purged on a 30-day clock without corrupting the restore chain for unrelated customer data. The controls are isolation plus a hard expiry plus re-deletion on restore. If 90 days is too long for you, offer us 60 days and we will accept it. What we will not accept is an indefinite backup carve-out or one that lets drawing data be accessed from backup outside a genuine recovery.

**3. Closeout and verification — records, fixtures, third parties**

Replace your closeout paragraph with:

> "Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the testing house must securely erase or destroy the drawings, CAD files, derived fixture geometry, working copies and physical prints in its possession or under its control, including copies held by approved third parties, subject only to the backup exception above and the record exception below.
>
> Record exception: the testing house may retain calibration, accreditation, quality and compliance records required by its accreditation body or by law — including calibration records retained for two years — and the accepted test report, provided none contains drawings or reconstructable geometry. On request the testing house will confirm in writing the categories retained and the expiry of each retention period.
>
> Fixtures: at the Design Owner's election, fixtures fabricated from interface geometry will be surrendered to the Design Owner in place of destruction; otherwise they must be destroyed by the same deadline. The certificate must state which option applied.
>
> Verification: by the same deadline the testing house will provide a certificate from an independent verifier, acceptable to both parties and bound by written confidentiality, identifying the materials destroyed, the methods and dates of destruction, the restoration events (if any), and any exceptions. The verifier may inspect records and destruction evidence but receives no CAD or reconstructable geometry and enters no site. This certificate satisfies the Design Owner's verification requirement; no site access, announced or unannounced, is granted, and none is available at the shared customer site in any event."

Why the changes: our accredited lab and our own accreditation require calibration records to be kept for two years. Those records are instrument and machine data — no geometry — so your deletion objective is not compromised; deleting them would put our accreditation at risk and would not protect your design. The fixture election matters because a destroyed fixture cannot be produced as evidence if the test results are later disputed; surrendering it to you protects your geometry better than destruction does. And on verification: we accept the certificate as the complete verification mechanism and will not accept any inspection right, on demand or otherwise, since the site is shared and our other customers' work is there.

Trade to close quickly: we take the 90-day backup carve-out and the two-year record retention; you get the extract limits, the no-competitor-use restriction, the independent verifier with no geometry, and fixture surrender on your election. Tell us 60 or 90 days on backups, and whether three or five business days on substitution objections, and we can finalise the attachments.

We accept **60 calendar days after the closeout deadline** for backup expiry and **three business days** for substitution objections. We accept your minimum-extract limits, the two-year retention of geometry-free calibration records, and the Design Owner’s option to take delivery of fixtures. We also accept independent certification as the complete verification mechanism, with no site access.

We propose the following wording for the substitution and backup provisions. Your other wording is acceptable, including the prohibition on reuse to develop competing products.

**Substitution.** “The testing house must give written notice naming each replacement individual, their firm, their task and the extract they need, together with their written undertaking to observe confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The three-business-day period starts on receipt of the complete notice. Access may begin on earlier written approval or when that period expires without a reasonable written objection. If the Design Owner objects within the period, access requires resolution of the objection in writing. Approval extends only to the named individuals and specified extracts. The testing house must revoke outgoing access on the date of notice and ensure that outgoing holders securely erase their working copies within 30 calendar days of notice. The independent verifier’s closeout certificate must cover those deletions.”

**Backups and proof of expiry.** “The backup exception applies only to encrypted, isolated disaster-recovery backups held by the testing house or an approved third party. They may be restored only for genuine disaster recovery. Restored drawing data must remain isolated from operational users until securely erased. Erasure must occur within ten business days of restoration and in all cases by the final backup expiry date, 60 calendar days after the closeout deadline. Restoration does not restart that period.

“The independent verifier’s 30-day closeout certificate must identify any backups still held, their scheduled expiry dates and any restoration and re-deletion events to date. If backups remain, the testing house must provide a supplemental certificate from the verifier within five business days after final expiry, confirming erasure and recording any intervening restoration and re-deletion events.”

For fixture surrender, we will make any election in writing when we accept the report or terminate the tests. In the absence of an election, destruction by the closeout deadline is the default. The verifier may rely on our receipt as evidence of surrender.

Two gaps in the wording as drafted, then we are closed. Everything else — substitution mechanics, the 60-day final expiry, the supplemental certificate, the fixture election and default — is agreed.

**1. Backup restoration is over-restricted.** "Restored only for genuine disaster recovery" would bar scheduled restore testing. Integrity verification of backups is required by our quality system and by accreditation expectations; forbidding it weakens recovery guarantees without protecting your geometry. Amend the first backup paragraph:

> "The backup exception applies only to encrypted, isolated disaster-recovery backups held by the testing house or an approved third party. They may be restored only for genuine disaster recovery or for scheduled verification of backup integrity. In either case, restoration occurs in an isolated environment not connected to operational systems, and restored drawing data must remain isolated from operational users until securely erased. Erasure must occur within ten business days of restoration and in all cases by the final backup expiry date, 60 calendar days after the closeout deadline. Restoration does not restart that period."

A restore-to-isolation for an integrity check is no more exposure than a disaster restore; both are subject to the same re-deletion clock.

**2. Timing gap on outgoing-holder deletions.** The substitution clause requires outgoing holders to erase within 30 calendar days of notice, but the closeout certificate is issued 30 days after report acceptance. A substitution late in the job can leave a deletion falling due after that certificate. Add to the substitution paragraph:

> "If an outgoing holder's deletion period ends after the closeout certificate is issued, that deletion must be confirmed in the supplemental certificate or, if no supplemental certificate is due, in a short-form certificate issued within ten business days after the deletion deadline."

And one sentence at the end of the backup paragraph to make the certificates workable where backup systems or third parties are involved:

> "For each certificate, the independent verifier may rely on the testing house's records, deletion logs and written attestations from operators of its systems and approved third parties; the verifier receives no drawing data or reconstructable geometry."

This keeps the verification burden on us and off your audit team: the verifier certifies on records and attestations, never geometry.

Your fixture mechanics are accepted as written: written election at report acceptance or on termination, destruction in the absence of election, your receipt as evidence of surrender.

Confirm these two amendments and the attachments are final: substitution with extracts and rolling deletion, backups at 60 days with integrity verification and no period restart, two-year geometry-free records, fixture surrender on your election, and independent certification as the complete verification mechanism with no site access.
We accept both amendments as drafted, including the verifier’s reliance on records, deletion logs and written attestations. The attachments are final on the agreed wording.

The coupon workflow is workable and we prefer it to sending the shop any geometry — the shop machines from a numbers-only tolerance table. To make it run cleanly, we need four things settled: tolerance specification, custody of the coupon and stock, signoff points, and the schedule.

**1. Workflow and tolerances.** Propose:

> "The Design Owner delivers written tolerances for the fixture interface within two business days of these terms being agreed. Within one business day of receipt, the test lead measures the reference coupon at the testing house on calibrated equipment and issues to the machining shop a tolerance table in tabular form. The shop machines the already-cut stock to that table and delivers the fixture to the testing house."

The two days on your side for tolerances matters: our shop's stock is already cut and the lead has the metrology slot booked. If tolerances arrive late, each day of lateness pushes the same day downstream.

**2. Extract and custody.** Define the table so it stays inside the approved extract limits:

> "The tolerance table contains only tabulated dimensional and tolerance values for the fixture interface. It contains no drawings, CAD, datum reference schemes, surface data, or other information from which the tested product's geometry can be reconstructed. It is a permitted extract for the machining shop under the agreed extract limits, logged in the extract records and subject to the same deletion and certification at closeout."

Custody:

> "The reference coupon remains at the testing house throughout and under its custody; it does not travel to the shop. After the fixture is accepted and the repeatability check passed, the coupon is returned to the machining shop as scrap stock or destroyed at the Design Owner's election, and is not used on any other project. The cut stock remains at the shop until machining and is treated as fixture material under the fixtures clause."

**3. Repeatability and signoff.** You asked us to work with your acceptance of a repeatability check; here is the mechanic:

> "The test lead performs two independent measurements of the coupon. If the spread is within the repeatability limit you specify with the tolerances, the test lead certifies the tolerance table and issues it. If the spread exceeds that limit, the lead re-measures; a second exceedance requires resolution with the Design Owner before the shop machines — the Design Owner may appoint a metrology witness or require accredited third-party measurement, with any resulting delay on the schedule below."

Signoff, given you have no site access and none is granted:

> "Before vibration testing begins, the test lead transmits to the Design Owner the fixture conformance data: measured fixture interface dimensions against the tolerance table and the repeatability results. Testing may begin on written approval or one business day after transmission without a reasonable written objection. Objection is limited to conformance with the specified tolerances."

That is your test signoff: conformance data out, approval or deemed approval in one business day. It keeps the geometry off your problem list too — you see numbers, not the fixture.

**4. The two-day delay.** Propose:

> "The agreed test start moves two business days from the previously scheduled date. Neither party is in breach by reason of that two-day slip. All downstream dates, including report acceptance and the closeout and backup expiry deadlines, are keyed to actual acceptance of the report and shift accordingly. Each day of delay attributable to late delivery of tolerances, failure of signoff, or a repeatability exceedance caused by the specified limits falls on the party whose act or omission caused it."

The last sentence is the trade: we carry the two days without argument because the shop's stock and the substitution route are our operational issues; you carry tolerance-and-signoff days, since only you can set and confirm them. If you want the two days absorbed as a no-fault slip with no causation split at all, we accept that, but then signoff must be one business day, not two.

We accept the numbers-only shop workflow, a two-business-day adjustment to the test start, and one-business-day signoff. For this batch, we propose the following narrow addendum.

**Release and machining.** “The Design Owner will withhold the restricted geometry on page 4 and supply a drawing set with that geometry removed. Within two business days of agreement on this addendum, the Design Owner will deliver to the testing house an alternative reference coupon, written interface tolerances and a repeatability limit. The Design Owner will verify before release that the coupon and permitted table values, taken together with the released drawings, do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the restricted geometry. The testing house will use only the released set. The shop will receive only the logged numbers-only table described in its proposal, subject to the agreed deletion and certification terms.”

**Verification and signoff.** “Within one business day of receiving the coupon and specifications, the named test lead will measure each specified interface dimension twice on calibrated equipment, removing and repositioning the coupon between measurements. The lead may certify and issue the table once the spread for each dimension meets its specified limit. After a failed check, the lead may repeat the pair of measurements. A second failure holds machining pending written agreement on the measurement method. Any additional reviewer must meet the agreed named-person access requirements.

“Before vibration testing, the lead will send the Design Owner the repeatability results and the measured fixture dimensions against each tolerance. Testing may begin on written approval or one business day after receipt of complete, passing results without a reasonable written objection concerning tolerance or repeatability. Any such objection must be resolved in writing before testing.”

**Custody.** “The coupon stays at the testing house under the named lead’s control through fixture acceptance. It may then be returned directly to the Design Owner at its written election. Otherwise the testing house must destroy it by the existing closeout deadline. The independent certificate will record return or destruction. The shop keeps the cut stock until machining and delivers the finished fixture to the testing house under the agreed fixture terms.” We require direct return or destruction because sending the coupon to the shop as scrap would defeat the table-only arrangement.

**Schedule.** We take your no-fault option. The scheduled start moves two business days, with neither party in breach for that adjustment. If verification requires more time, the parties will record the resulting revised dates in writing. Closeout remains tied to actual written report acceptance or earlier termination, and the 60-calendar-day backup expiry runs from that closeout deadline.

Please confirm these terms so the project engineer can prepare the coupon and reserve the metrology slot against the revised start.

Three clarifications, then confirmed. The workflow, the two-business-day schedule move with no breach, the one-business-day signoff with repeat-and-hold mechanics, the custody rules, and the closeout tie-in are all acceptable as drafted.

**1. Substitution must reach this addendum.** "Named test lead," "additional reviewer" and shop personnel cannot be read to freeze named people for the batch, since the master attachments allow substitution by notice with three business days to object. Add to the verification paragraph:

> "References to the named test lead are to the lead appointed under the substitution provisions of the master attachments. Those provisions apply to the lead, any reviewer and shop personnel, and a replacement assumes the role on appointment. If the lead changes, custody of the coupon and control of the released materials pass to the replacement lead on appointment, and the outgoing lead's deletion and certification obligations cover any working copies."

Without this, a single absence could hold machining while a fresh approval is negotiated outside the agreed mechanism.

**2. The logged table and the measurement records.** The shop's log and our verification measurements are numbers-only, but they must be classified under the existing closeout and record terms so no one argues later that they are derived geometry. Add to the release paragraph:

> "The logged numbers-only table, the repeatability results and the measured fixture dimensions are derived materials under the closeout terms and will be deleted under them, except that the testing house may retain calibration, accreditation and quality records of the verification measurements under the existing record exception. No record retained will contain drawings or reconstructable geometry."

**3. Objection default on the signoff.** Your one-day signoff clock and the testing start default are agreed. One sentence to keep the two clocks consistent, since the lead issues the table on certification but testing waits on your side:

> "The one-business-day period for issuing the table runs on our side alone; the one-business-day objection period runs only on receipt of complete, passing results. If the results are incomplete, the objection period does not start, and the schedule adjustment provisions apply."

This prevents a dispute about whether a partial submission started your clock.

Your custody rule is accepted as drafted: coupon stays under the lead's control through fixture acceptance, direct return at your written election, destruction by the closeout deadline otherwise, no scrap route to the shop, and the independent certificate records return or destruction. The verifier may rely on our records and the shop's attestation on the cut stock and finished fixture as under the master attachments.

Confirm these three sentences and the addendum is final. On that confirmation the project engineer can prepare the coupon and reserve the metrology slot against the revised start.

We confirm all three clarifications as proposed. The addendum is final for this prototype batch.

A replacement lead assumes custody when the appointment takes effect under the master substitution procedure. The table and measurement results are subject to closeout deletion, with retention limited to records that qualify under the existing exception and contain no drawings or reconstructable geometry. The testing house’s one-business-day table deadline remains subject to the repeat-and-hold procedure. The Design Owner’s one-business-day objection period begins only on receipt of complete, passing results.

The project engineer can proceed with coupon preparation and reserve the metrology slot for the revised start.

Two points need reconciling before our engineer acts on this, because the addendum we finalised does not contain the terms you reference.

1. **Unmatched terms.** The "one-business-day table deadline," the "repeat-and-hold procedure" and the "one-business-day objection period" on complete, passing results are not in the addendum we closed, and the Design Owner's objection right we agreed is three business days on substitution notices. If these are project-schedule arrangements for this batch, send the operative wording or the schedule reference and we will treat them as scheduling terms only — not as amendments to the access, deletion or verification attachments. What we will not do is let an undefined "repeat-and-hold" procedure alter the deletion clock, the extract limits or the certificate deadlines. Please confirm: (a) the repeat-and-hold procedure does not extend closeout or backup expiry dates, and (b) a held or repeated run produces no additional extract beyond the approved ones.

2. **Results table treatment.** Consistent with the record exception, we will delete the raw table and measurement results at closeout except to the extent the accepted test report — which we may retain — includes them and contains no drawings or reconstructable geometry. A tabulated results set with no geometry qualifies for retention as part of that report; if you want the raw table excluded from the retained report, say so now and we will record that election in the attachments.

Custody transfer of a replacement lead under the master substitution procedure is accepted as stated: custody passes on the effective date of the appointment, with revocation and deletion obligations running per the substitution clause. Coupon preparation and metrology slot reservation will proceed on the revised start once we have the wording under point 1, so the schedule is not exposed to a later dispute about what "passing results" triggers the objection clock.

We confirm both points under item 1. A repeat or hold grants no extension to closeout, backup expiry or certificate deadlines. Those dates follow the existing triggers of written report acceptance or earlier termination. A repeat or hold authorizes no additional extract. The shop receives only the approved numbers-only interface table.

Please use the following operative wording in the **batch schedule**:

> Within one business day after receiving the coupon, written tolerances and repeatability limits, the test lead will measure each specified dimension twice on calibrated equipment, removing and repositioning the coupon between readings. If the absolute difference for each pair is within its specified limit, the lead will certify and issue the approved table within that same business day. If a pair fails, the lead will withhold the table and repeat the failed pair once. A second failure holds machining until the parties agree in writing on the measurement method and the lead obtains passing results.
>
> Before vibration testing, the lead will send the Design Owner the paired readings, their differences and applicable limits, and the measured fixture dimensions against each specified tolerance. Results are complete and passing when they cover every specified dimension and meet every applicable limit and tolerance. Testing may begin on written approval or one business day after the Design Owner receives complete, passing results without a reasonable written objection concerning tolerance or repeatability. Any such objection must be resolved in writing before testing.

The three-business-day objection period continues to govern personnel substitutions. The one-business-day period governs only the start of vibration testing for this batch.

For item 2, **we elect to exclude the raw interface table and raw measurement results from the retained report**, including its appendices. The report may retain a pass/fail summary and vibration-test outcomes that contain no drawings or reconstructable geometry. The existing exception for required calibration, accreditation and quality records remains available on its agreed terms.

Coupon preparation and metrology slot reservation may proceed on the revised schedule.

The batch schedule wording is acceptable. Two clarifications keep it workable without changing the bargain, and both stay within what we have already agreed.

**1. Nonconformance records.** Failed-pair readings, repeat results and any second-failure hold documentation are quality records — our accreditation and the accredited laboratory's require retention of nonconformance and corrective-action records. They contain only numbers, limits and dates, no geometry. Confirm they fall within the existing calibration, accreditation and quality records exception; we will list them in the categories confirmed on request, and the pass/fail summary in the retained report remains the only drawing-free summary of the outcome. The raw interface table and raw passing measurements are excluded from the retained report as you elected and are erased at closeout on the agreed terms.

**2. Metrology clock.** One business day from receipt is workable only with the slot confirmed, and a failed intermediate calibration check on the day would breach the schedule through no fault of ours. Replace the opening of the first paragraph with:

> "Within one business day after the testing house receives the coupon, the written tolerances and repeatability limits, and confirmation of the reserved metrology slot, the test lead will measure each specified dimension twice on calibrated equipment, removing and repositioning the coupon between readings. If calibrated equipment becomes unavailable through no fault of the testing house, including a failed intermediate check, the period runs from the next day that calibrated equipment is available, and the test lead will notify the Design Owner promptly in writing."

The remainder of the paragraph and the second paragraph are accepted exactly as drafted. So is your confirmation that a repeat or hold extends no deadline, authorizes no additional extract, and that the shop receives only the approved numbers-only interface table. The three-business-day period governs personnel substitution; the one-business-day period governs only the start of vibration testing for this batch.

Confirm these two points and the batch schedule is final.

We confirm both points and accept the proposed metrology wording as written. The batch schedule is final.

Failed-pair readings, repeat results and second-failure hold documentation qualify under the existing records exception to the extent required for accreditation or by law. The testing house and accredited laboratory may retain the required records for the applicable retention period, provided they contain no drawings or reconstructable geometry. The testing house will identify the retained categories and their expiry dates on request. The retained report may include a pass/fail summary of fixture verification. The raw interface table and raw readings remain excluded from the report.

The one-business-day measurement period begins upon receipt of the coupon, written tolerances, repeatability limits and confirmation of the reserved slot. If calibrated equipment becomes unavailable through no fault of the testing house, the lead will notify the Design Owner promptly in writing, and the period runs from the next day calibrated equipment is available. Coupon preparation and slot reservation may proceed on the agreed schedule.

We have no metrology wording or batch schedule on the table in this exchange. What we have finalised is limited to the substitution, extract, backup, fixture, closeout and verification attachments — the attachments named in our last confirmation. We cannot confirm terms as written that we have not seen or drafted.

Please send the actual text of the metrology wording and the batch schedule you want attached, including: the scope of the fixture verification, the coupon and interface table definitions, the repeatability limits and how they are set, and where the one-business-day measurement period sits in the overall test schedule. Once we have that text we will review it against the agreed record and extract limits — in particular the prohibition on retained material containing reconstructable geometry, which already constrains any "interface table" and "raw readings" you may intend to keep outside the report.

On the substance you have described, two constraints are already fixed and will carry into whatever metrology wording you send: deletion and record-retention obligations run from the agreed closeout mechanics, not from a separate metrology clock; and no retained category may expand the exception beyond records required for accreditation or by law and the accepted report, each geometry-free. The pass/fail summary in the retained report is consistent with that; raw readings and raw interface tables are not, and any retention of those would need to fit the existing exception or be excluded.

We are not agreeing a one-business-day measurement period or an equipment-unavailability tolling mechanism without the text. Send the wording and schedule and we will respond on the terms.

**Proposed attachment — prototype batch fixture verification and test schedule**

1. **Purpose and release.** This attachment applies only to this batch. Verification covers the repeatability of coupon measurements and the finished fixture’s conformance to the specified interface tolerances. The Design Owner will withhold the restricted geometry on page 4 and supply a drawing set with that geometry removed. Before release, the Design Owner will verify that the released drawings, coupon and permitted table values, considered together, do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the restricted geometry.

2. **Coupon and table.** The reference coupon is an alternative physical measurement reference prepared by the Design Owner for use at the testing house. The interface table is the test lead’s certified list of dimensional values and tolerances needed to machine the fixture from the already-cut stock. The shop receives only the logged table. It contains no drawings, CAD, datum reference schemes, surface data or information from which the product geometry can be reconstructed. The coupon remains at the testing house under the named lead’s control. The master substitution procedure applies to the lead, reviewers and shop personnel. Coupon custody transfers when a replacement lead’s appointment takes effect.

3. **Schedule and limits.** The scheduled vibration-test start moves two business days from the previously scheduled date. Neither party is in breach by reason of that adjustment. Within two business days of agreement on this attachment, the Design Owner will deliver the coupon and a written specification listing, for each interface dimension, its identifier, units, permissible fixture tolerance and numerical repeatability limit. The repeatability limit is the maximum permitted absolute difference between two independent coupon readings. The project engineer will arrange the metrology slot for the revised schedule.

4. **Measurement and table release.** Within one business day after the testing house receives the coupon, written tolerances and repeatability limits, and confirmation of the reserved metrology slot, the test lead will measure each specified dimension twice on calibrated equipment, removing and repositioning the coupon between readings. If calibrated equipment becomes unavailable through no fault of the testing house, including a failed intermediate calibration check, the lead will promptly notify the Design Owner in writing. The period then runs from the next day calibrated equipment is available. If every pair meets its limit, the lead will certify and issue the table within the measurement period. If a pair fails, the lead will withhold the table and repeat that pair once. A second failure holds machining until the parties agree in writing on the measurement method and the lead obtains passing results. The shop may then machine the stock to the certified table and deliver the fixture to the testing house.

5. **Signoff before vibration testing.** The lead will send the Design Owner the paired readings, their differences and applicable limits, and the measured fixture dimensions against the specified tolerances. Complete, passing results must cover every specified dimension and demonstrate compliance with each repeatability limit and fixture tolerance. Testing may begin on written approval or one business day after receipt of complete, passing results without a reasonable written objection concerning tolerance or repeatability. Any such objection requires written resolution before testing. If verification requires more time, the parties will record revised project dates in writing. A repeat or hold authorizes no additional extract and grants no extension to the closeout, backup expiry or certificate deadlines.

6. **Disposition and records.** After fixture acceptance, the testing house will return the coupon directly to the Design Owner upon written election or destroy it by the existing closeout deadline. The independent certificate will record its disposition. The master fixture clause governs the finished fixture. The interface table, measurement results and working copies held by the testing house or its third parties fall under the master closeout terms. The retained report may include the fixture pass/fail summary and geometry-free vibration-test outcomes. It must exclude the raw table and raw readings, including in appendices. Failed-pair readings, repeat results and corrective-action or hold records may be retained separately only to the extent and for the period required by accreditation or law. Every retained record, including the accepted report, must be free of drawings and reconstructable geometry. On request, the testing house will identify the retained categories and their expiry dates.

The master attachments govern access, deletion, backup expiry and independent certification throughout. Please confirm this text for attachment to the batch schedule.

The attachment structure is acceptable. Three points need adjustment before we confirm; all three concern timing or records, not the substance of verification.

**1. Measurement period does not run from the right event.** Paragraph 4 starts the one-business-day measurement period on receipt of the coupon, tolerances and "confirmation of the reserved metrology slot." If the project engineer confirms a slot for a later date, the period expires before the slot occurs. Replace the opening of paragraph 4 with:

> "Within one business day after the later of (a) the reserved metrology slot date and (b) the testing house's receipt of the coupon, the written tolerances and repeatability limits, the test lead will measure each specified dimension twice on calibrated equipment... If the specification lists more than 20 interface dimensions, the period is two business days."

The count threshold is a scheduling reality: each dimension requires a full remove-and-reposition cycle on calibrated equipment. If the actual dimension list is short, the threshold never engages and you lose nothing.

**2. Deleting the readings leaves no defence record.** Paragraph 6 sends the interface table and measurement results to deletion at the closeout deadline, with the accepted report keeping only a pass/fail summary. If the fixture's conformance or the test results are later disputed, neither party will have the underlying data. The pair readings and certified table are dimension values and differences only — by the Design Owner's own characterisation in paragraph 2, they contain no reconstructable product geometry. Amend paragraph 6:

> "The interface table and the paired measurement results may be retained as quality and compliance records for 24 months from acceptance of the test report, falling under the master record exception, since they contain no drawings or reconstructable geometry. They remain subject to the master use restrictions and may not be used for another project. All other working copies fall under the master closeout terms and are deleted by the closeout deadline. The raw table and raw readings remain excluded from the accepted report."
